title: Governance, Risk and Compliance, Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery

header.html: 2.1 Plan Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC): Purpose; Importance; Frameworks and tools. 2.2 Understand redundancy: Business Continuity (BC); Disaster Recovery (DR)
the official ISC2 CC exam outline

toc.title: Testing the plans and the AI angle

html:
1Governance, risk and compliance (GRC)

GRC brings three things together so the organization reaches its goals reliably, manages uncertainty and acts with integrity.

Part Question Example
Governance Who decides, and what is the direction? Board-approved security strategy and policies
Risk What could go wrong, and how bad? Risk register and treatment plans
Compliance Are we following the rules? Audits against laws, standards and policies
Point Fact
Purpose Align security with business goals, manage risk, prove compliance
Importance Avoid fines and loss, make informed decisions, build trust
Frameworks and tools NIST CSF, ISO/IEC 27001, COBIT; GRC platforms that hold the risk register, policies, evidence and audit tasks
Exam tip

. GRC is one program, not three. Its goal is decisions based on risk that also meet the rules.

2Business continuity and disaster recovery

Plan Scope Goal
Business continuity plan (BCP) The whole business: people, process, sites Keep critical functions running during a disruption
Disaster recovery plan (DRP) IT systems and data Restore them after a disaster
Incident response plan (IRP) A security incident Detect, contain and recover (Module 15)

A business impact analysis (BIA) comes first: it finds the critical functions, their dependencies and the cost of downtime.

Metric Meaning
Maximum tolerable downtime (MTD) (or MAO) The longest outage the business can survive
Recovery time objective (RTO) The target time to restore a system; shorter than the MTD
Recovery point objective (RPO) The most data you can lose, measured in time since the last backup
Exam tip

. RTO = how long to be back. RPO = how much data to lose. BIA first, then the plans.

3Redundancy and recovery options

Item Fact
Redundancy Spare capacity so one failure does not stop service: RAID, clustering, failover, load balancing, dual power, UPS and generators
Hot site Fully equipped and running; recovery in minutes to hours; most expensive
Warm site Equipment ready, data must be loaded; hours to days
Cold site Space and power only; days to weeks; cheapest
Cloud recovery Rebuild in the cloud on demand
Backup type What it copies Restore needs
Full Everything The latest full backup
Differential Changes since the last full Last full plus the latest differential
Incremental Changes since the last backup of any kind Last full plus every incremental since

3-2-1 rule: three copies, on two kinds of media, one off site. A backup you have not tested is a hope, not a plan.

4Testing the plans and the AI angle

Test What happens Disruption
Read-through or checklist Team reads the plan None
Tabletop (walkthrough) Team talks through a scenario None
Simulation Acts out a scenario Low
Parallel Systems are recovered at the alternate site while production runs Low
Full interruption Production is shut down and the alternate site takes over High

AI and recovery: back up AI configurations and datasets, not only traditional data. Model drift, a decline in AI performance over time, is a business continuity risk because operations that rely on the model suffer.

Exam tip

. Tabletop exercises are discussion only; full interruption is the riskiest test. Hot = fast and costly; cold = slow and cheap.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A company must be able to lose no more than one hour of data after a failure. Which metric states this requirement?

  • ARecovery time objective of one hour
  • BMaximum tolerable downtime of one hour
  • CRecovery point objective of one hour
  • DAnnualized loss expectancy of one hour
Show the answer

Answer: C. The recovery point objective is the maximum acceptable data loss measured in time.

S2Which plan focuses on keeping the critical functions of the whole business running during a disruption?

  • AThe disaster recovery plan, which restores IT systems
  • BThe business continuity plan, which covers the business
  • CThe incident response plan, which handles security events
  • DThe risk register, which lists the identified risks
Show the answer

Answer: B. The business continuity plan covers the whole business; the disaster recovery plan restores IT.

S3A bank needs a recovery site that can take over within minutes and accepts the highest cost. Which site fits?

  • AA cold site with space and power only
  • BA hot site that is fully equipped and running
  • CA warm site with equipment and no data
  • DA mobile site that is trucked to the location
Show the answer

Answer: B. A hot site is ready to take over within minutes to hours and is the most expensive option.

S4Which analysis should be done first to find the critical business functions and the cost of downtime?

  • APenetration test of the network
  • BVulnerability scan of the servers
  • CSecurity awareness training review
  • DBusiness impact analysis
Show the answer

Answer: D. The business impact analysis identifies critical functions and drives the recovery objectives.

S5A team reads a scenario aloud around a table and decides who would do what, without touching any system. What type of test is this?

  • ATabletop exercise that only discusses the scenario
  • BFull interruption test of the alternate site
  • CParallel test that recovers systems at the alternate site
  • DSimulation that runs the recovery steps on test servers
Show the answer

Answer: A. A tabletop or walkthrough exercise is a discussion and does not disrupt operations.

S6A company uses an AI model to approve orders, and over several months the model's accuracy falls. Which risk does this describe?

  • AVendor lock-in, a risk of the contract
  • BPrivilege creep, a risk of the identity life cycle process
  • CModel drift, a continuity risk for the operation
  • DTailgating, a risk of the building entry
Show the answer

Answer: C. Model drift is a decline in AI performance that can harm operations, so it belongs in continuity planning.

5.2 Recall questions

R1What does RTO measure?

Show the answer

The target time to restore a system.

R2Which site is the cheapest and slowest?

Show the answer

A cold site.

R3What does the 3-2-1 rule say?

Show the answer

Three copies, two media, one off site.

R4What must be restored after a differential backup?

Show the answer

The last full backup plus the latest differential.

R5What comes before the BCP and DRP?

Show the answer

The business impact analysis.

R6Which test shuts production down?

Show the answer

The full interruption test.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
GRC governance (direction), risk, compliance; one program
Plans BCP (business), DRP (IT), IRP (security incident)
Metrics MTD (longest outage), RTO (time back), RPO (data loss)
Sites hot (fast, costly), warm, cold (slow, cheap)
Backups full, differential, incremental; 3-2-1; test restores
Tests read-through, tabletop, simulation, parallel, full interruption
AI back up configs and datasets; model drift is a risk
